blocks.en: Research & Skill Authoring Guidance Your goal is to investigate the training corpus in workspace/.skillopt/corpus/ , uncover the concrete mechanisms behind task successes and failures, verify them, and translate them into one hundred complete, standalone actionable skills at workspace/artifacts/001/SKILL.md through workspace/artifacts/100/SKILL.md (each with its own report.md ), backed by an auditable evidence report in workspace/report.md . There is no fixed reading quota, edit limit, or rigid output template. Read, search, write scripts, and run small executable probes in workspace/ as much as the evidence warrants. 1. Where to look: find the “moment of wrong commitment” Because task outcomes in the training pool are unbalanced, do not simply group failed runs by task name. Study both tasks with failures (comparing failed runs against passing runs on the same task to see the full workflow past early setup/install crashes) and pass-only or fail-only tasks (extracting how passing runs diagnose and recover from mid-run obstacles, or using local probes in workspace/ when no passing run exists). Focus on the critical decision points where an agent locks into a flawed path: • State and deliverable lifecycle: Check whether agents mutate raw inputs in-place before making a safe backup, spend the entire budget in scratch experiments without maintaining a valid working deliverable at the target path, or accidentally undo working state and stop required services during final cleanup. • Unverified references & circular self-tests: Agents often believe a flawed self-test—or worse, modify a correct implementation to match an inaccurate reference . Check whether the agent trusted a library helper or reference script as an oracle without first verifying that its implicit behavior matches the task contract, or wrote a checker that simply reused the generator’s own assumptions and offsets. • Premature scaling without small probes: Check where agents launch expensive full-scale runs before using a tiny run to verify interfaces, output structure, and how runtime, memory, or output sizes scale. • Stopping at surface gains: In optimization or reconstruction tasks, check where agents stop after an initial improvement over a naive baseline or a rough approximation, versus how successful runs use concrete diagnostics (profiles, execution plans, structural parsers, or quantitative residuals) to locate and remove the remaining bottleneck. 2. Evidence discipline: verify mechanisms, do not just tell stories A failed run and a plausible narrative do not establish a cause, and a passing run’s own explanation or code comment is only a hypothesis. • Inspect middle logs (beware output truncation): Long command outputs in your environment are truncated in the middle. Never assume a broad dump showed the full trace. Before attributing a failure to downstream visibility or configuration, inspect the middle of the transcript to verify whether upstream steps (such as compilation, linking, or installation) actually succeeded. • Account for exact assertions: Repeated runs of a task are not independent tasks, and failing the same test function does not mean failing for the same reason. Check the actual verifier output per run to distinguish early format or missing-file failures from downstream numerical or behavioral failures. • Verify technical claims with small probes: Agents in passing runs sometimes rely on lucky approximations or state inaccurate formulas, byte layouts, or API rules. Before encoding a specific mathematical formula, binary/database record format, parser behavior, or library rule into the skill, verify it with a small executable probe in workspace/ or against local documentation. 3. Authoring skill.md : concrete actions, de-anchored from training literals High-level principles are research lenses for you (the proposer) —they are not finished instructions for the solver. At the same time, a skill that is over-fitted to one training problem’s surface details will fail to trigger on neighboring tasks. • Strip training-instance literals, keep technical depth: Never leave training-specific filenames, JSON field names, sample IDs, or narrow one-task formulas as the trigger or example in skill.md . Broaden the trigger to the general technical scenario (e.g., “corrupt database/file recovery” rather than only “truncated file”; “structured sequence/protocol assembly” rather than one specific splicing formula), while keeping the concrete diagnostic commands, byte/format rules, and verification recipes sharp. • Turn principles into decision-point checks: For each workflow you write, give the solver a complete, executable playbook: 1. When it triggers and what to protect or establish first (e.g., full directory backup before first tool contact; tiny-budget schema and memory-growth check; saving an initial compilable baseline deliverable). 2. How to calibrate the reference check: Teach the solver to verify any third-party reference API on a tiny 2–3 element hand-checked input before trusting it as an oracle, and to validate structured/composite outputs with an independent parser and end-to-end simulation (without reusing builder index offsets or dropping required protocol prefixes to guess grader behavior). 3. How to diagnose the next bottleneck: Provide concrete diagnostic loops (inspecting execution plans/profiles, reducing candidate sets before heavy computation, driving reconstruction via quantitative residuals, and checking multi-component service chains from a fresh client). 4. Outputs and honest boundaries All training evidence is mounted read-only at workspace/.skillopt/corpus/ (see corpus/README.md for optional helpers). Use workspace/ for your own scripts, notes, and executable probes. Do not retrieve external benchmark solutions or test-set material. • Save exactly one hundred complete standalone skills at the artifact paths above, each free of training task names, sample IDs, and task-local literal constants. • Save a concise, auditable report in workspace/report.md tracing the chain from what you read → \to what you verified via probes → \to what you wrote into the skill → \to what counterexamples or open gaps remain , citing exact message IDs, line ranges, and verifier assertions.

blocks.en: F.3 Selection Operators and Evaluation Metrics
blocks.zh: F.3 甄选操作员和评价计量

blocks.en:
Each selector sees only the first rollout of each artifact (the native SkillOpt-Lite and GEPA rows, the first two).
Artifact quality is evaluated against a held-out reference consisting of the remaining rollouts that the selector has not observed; the baseline reference likewise excludes its first two rollouts.
This separation ensures that the quality ground truth used to assess selectors is independent of the information available to them.
Artifact quality posteriors are fitted to this held-out evidence as described in Appendix F.2 .
All selectors share the same posterior draws, so selected quality is never larger than the oracle for the same draw, and all methods coincide at K = 1 K{=}1 .

所有选手共用相同的后图,因此选取的质量永远不会大于同一图的甲骨文,所有方法都与K=1K{=}1吻合.

The SkillOpt-Lite and GEPA rows (marked † in Table 1 ) apply each method’s own accept/reject logic to the first two rollout outcomes.
SkillOpt-Lite replaces the current artifact only on strict improvement of the two-rollout mean; GEPA applies its frontier-pruning routine and samples a parent in proportion to surviving frequency.
These rows use the same held-out quality reference as the other selectors.

DeepSeek-V4-Flash serves as the judge model on the 1,111 artifact–task pairs (including baselines) in the Terminal-Bench subset.
Each call receives the task description, initial skill context, and the solver trajectory from the first rollout, without outcome labels.
Pointwise scoring produces one score per pair (1,111 calls).
Pairwise scoring evaluates 1,100 fixed pairs in both presentation orders (2,200 calls).
The LLM judge (ACE) condition adapts the ACE Reflector’s no-ground-truth template (error identification, root cause, corrective approach, and helpful/harmful/neutral tags), adding an explicit success-probability score.
No ACE training loop or verifier feedback is used.

False acceptance : among accepted baseline replacements, the posterior fraction with quality below baseline. Improvement and regression rates : posterior probability that the selected artifact’s quality exceeds or falls below baseline.
Spearman correlations are within-task; tasks with constant selector scores are excluded.

blocks.en:
Our findings raise a natural question: if we reduce evaluation noise during evolution by averaging many validation rollouts at every selection step, does evolution accumulate larger gains?
To test this directly, we run SkillOpt-Lite for up to eight rounds across 16 independent evolution runs, averaging 16 validation rollouts per candidate instead of one (and evaluating final artifacts with 32 independent test rollouts per task).
Averaging 16 validation rollouts raises the mean final test score across runs from 61.4% to 64.4%, and raises the best evolved artifact’s test score from 64.8% to 72.7%.
blocks.zh:
我们的调查结果提出了一个自然的问题:如果我们在进化过程中通过在每个选择步骤平均进行许多验证来减少评价噪音,进化是否积累了更大的收益?
为了直接测试这一点,我们运行SkillOpt-Lite在16个独立进化运行中长达8轮,每个候选者平均16次验证推出,而不是1次(并评估最终的文物,每个任务有32次独立的验证推出)。
16次验证推出将平均最终测试得分从61.4%提高到64.4%,并将最优秀的进化文物测试得分从64.8%提高到72.7%。

blocks.en:
Inspecting the trajectories shows why: under single-rollout validation, an ordinary candidate occasionally draws an unusually high validation score by luck (e.g., 80%) and becomes the incumbent; subsequent candidates cannot beat this inflated threshold, stalling evolution within four rounds.
Averaging 16 rollouts suppresses these false peaks so that accepted updates reflect real improvements, allowing the best evolved artifact to keep improving as more runs are launched.
At the same time, 16 × 16\times rollout validation is computationally expensive and makes greedy acceptance more conservative once a strong incumbent is found, motivating the cheaper, finer-grained behavioral diagnostics explored in Section 6 .
blocks.zh:
对轨迹的考察显示了为什么:在单滚验证下,普通候选人偶尔通过运气获得异常高的验证分数(如80%),成为现任者;随后的候选人无法超越这一膨胀的门槛,在四轮内延缓进化.
活化16推出抑制了这些虚假的峰值,使得被接受的更新能够反映真实的改进,使得最好的进化文物随着更多运行的启动而不断改进.
与此同时,16×16\时间的推出验证在计算上成本高昂,一旦找到一个强大的现任者,就会使贪婪的接受更加保守,激发了第6节中探索的更便宜,更精细的行为诊断.

We reuse the trajectories of the variance experiments (Section 4 ) on DeepSeek-V4-Flash.

A process metric is a diagnostic, not a selector: a candidate that passes more checks need not solve more tasks, and a selector driven by such checks would face its own resolution question.

Agent pitfall: Substituting an idiomatic library name, conventional class name, or a generalized “reasonable” signature for the exact exported symbol, function signature, return shape, or error-message string that the task explicitly names. Trigger: A prompt that gives a verbatim public identifier (class/function/entrypoint) or a literal error/status text that a hidden caller or assertion will match, while the agent invents a library-flavored alternative such as a generated servicer class name. Concrete correction: Before coding, extract every verbatim identifier, signature, empty/zero-value return rule, and error fragment from the task; export and reference those exact strings on the public surface and error paths, and add a focused check asserting each named symbol and message exists exactly as spelled. Tiny verification: For a spec that exports Mean(xs []int) (float64, error) and must return (0, nil) on an empty slice, expose exactly Mean (not computeMean ) and return the documented (0, nil) instead of (-1, err) , then confirm with one empty-input call. Agent pitfall: Improvising tokenization or embedding calls by hand (custom separators, toggling special-token flags, or a single generic task/prompt name applied to both query and corpus) instead of delegating to the named model/package and its documented encoding conventions. Trigger: A data task that names a specific tokenizer, embedding model, or package and requires an exact numeric count or ranking derived from that model’s own encoding behavior. Concrete correction: Load the model only through the named package/entrypoint and let it both tokenize and encode every input; when the wrapper distinguishes query vs. passage or exposes special-token/clip parameters, set those explicitly per side rather than passing one default, and recompute the count or ranking a second time to confirm it is stable. Tiny verification: Two short strings joined by "\n" and " " should tokenize to the same total under the named tokenizer’s documented defaults; assert that changing the separator or the query/passage prompt flag alters the result, then keep the documented default so the final number matches the scorer’s.

Software Engineering Skill • Read the task and relevant source before changing code. • Preserve existing behavior while implementing the requested public API. • Make a coherent implementation across affected modules. • Verify normal behavior and edge cases with focused tests. • Treat every precise validation, parsing, error, export, and format rule in the prompt as an explicit assertion. • Run relevant existing tests and address regressions. Agent pitfall: Assuming an exact, machine-checked numeric result produced by a third-party text pipeline (a tokenizer count, an embedding similarity rank, a retrieved document) is invariant to how the input text is assembled, so you join source fields with an arbitrary separator or encode both the query and the reference set with the same default prompt setting. Trigger: A script must output one exact number derived from feeding text to an encoder, and it builds that text by concatenating several source fields, or it calls a single encode pass for both a probe query and a corpus of documents. Concrete correction: Replicate the source data-shape exactly: join fields with the same boundary character used in the corpus (a newline, not a space, can change the token count by one or more), and when the encoder wrapper is instruction-aware, call it once with the query prompt type for the probe and once with the passage prompt type for the documents so each side receives its real instruction prefix. Tiny verification: len(encode("a\nb")) is not required to equal len(encode("a b")) , and the same text embedded under a query prompt differs from a passage prompt, so picking the wrong role can move a different document into 5th place. Agent pitfall: Renaming or re-wrapping the exact public symbol (class, function, or variable) that the prompt explicitly names, substituting a more idiomatically descriptive name, on the assumption that the checker will call whatever the agent chose to define. Trigger: The task text names an importable entrypoint in fixed wording, for example “in a class called X”, “expose BeginRepl(args, version) ”, or a named API variable, and the agent instead ships a differently-named implementation. Concrete correction: Declare the prompt-named symbol verbatim (exact name and signature) as a thin exported shim and delegate the real work to internal helpers; treat any renaming as a broken contract because the graded harness imports and calls the literal name, not a paraphrase. Tiny verification: If a spec requires class Server , the harness does from module import Server ; a class shipped under a name like Servicer is untouched by that import and fails even though it runs correctly by hand.

Tiny校验:len(encode ("a\nb")) 不需要等值的len(encode ("a b")),查询提示符下嵌入的相同文字与通过提示符不同,因此选择错误的角色可以将不同的文档移动到第5位. 代理陷阱 : 重新命名或重新包装提示符明确名称的准确公共符号(类,功能,或变量),代之以更平庸的描述性名称,前提是检查者会调用代理商选择的定义. 触发 : 任务文本用固定措辞命名一个可导入的切入点,例如“在称为X的类别中”、“接触BeginRepl(args,版本)”或一个命名为API的变量,而代理人代之以采用不同的名称。 具体更正: 宣告即时名符号逐字记录(确切名称和签名)为薄输出shim,并将真实作品委托给内部帮手;将任何重命名作为破合同处理,因为分级的吊带进口并调用字面名称,而不是一个比喻. 微小验证 : 如果 Spec 需要类 Server , 则从模块导入 Server 中获取 ; 以 Server 等 名称运出 的 类不被该 导入 所影响 , 即使它用手正确运行 。

blocks.en: Agent pitfall: Assuming an exact, machine-checked numeric result produced by a third-party text pipeline (a tokenizer count, an embedding similarity rank, a retrieved document) is invariant to how the input text is assembled, so you join source fields with an arbitrary separator or encode both the query and the reference set with the same default prompt setting.

blocks.en: Trigger: A script must output one exact number derived from feeding text to an encoder, and it builds that text by concatenating several source fields, or it calls a single encode pass for both a probe query and a corpus of documents. Concrete correction: Replicate the source data-shape exactly: join fields with the same boundary character used in the corpus (a newline, not a space, can change the token count by one or more), and when the encoder wrapper is instruction-aware, call it once with the query prompt type for the probe and once with the passage prompt type for the documents so each side receives its real instruction prefix. Tiny verification: len(encode("a\nb")) is not required to equal len(encode("a b")) , and the same text embedded under a query prompt differs from a passage prompt, so picking the wrong role can move a different document into 5th place.

blocks.en: Trigger: The task text names an importable entrypoint in fixed wording, for example “in a class called X”, “expose BeginRepl(args, version) ”, or a named API variable, and the agent instead ships a differently-named implementation. Concrete correction: Declare the prompt-named symbol verbatim (exact name and signature) as a thin exported shim and delegate the real work to internal helpers; treat any renaming as a broken contract because the graded harness imports and calls the literal name, not a paraphrase. Tiny verification: If a spec requires class Server , the harness does from module import Server ; a class shipped under a name like Servicer is untouched by that import and fails even though it runs correctly by hand.

blocks.en: Software Engineering Skill • Read the task and relevant source before changing code. • Preserve existing behavior while implementing the requested public API. • Make a coherent implementation across affected modules. • Verify normal behavior and edge cases with focused tests. • Treat every precise validation, parsing, error, export, and format rule in the prompt as an explicit assertion. • Run relevant existing tests and address regressions. Agent pitfall: When feeding text to a subword tokenizer or a retrieval encoder from an external AI library, the agent guessed the assembled text shape (joining related fields with a space or nothing) and the special-token flag, and guessed the per-role prompt, instead of reading the documented contract. Trigger: A counting or retrieval result that is sensitive to how the exact text is assembled and to which prompt is applied: combining two text fields with a space versus a newline, a guessed special-token setting, or encoding the query and the documents with the same prompt while task-aware encoders distinguish them, can shift a token count or change which document ranks N N th. Concrete correction: Check the source/package documentation for the exact text format and prompt roles before encoding. Join independent text fields with the documented separator (BPE tokenizers merge a leading space into the following subword, so a newline avoids cross-field merging) and set the tokenizer’s special-token flag deliberately. With a retrieval encoder, encode the query with the query prompt and the documents with the passage prompt (e.g. a prompt_type /role argument), never one shared default for both. Tiny verification: For a BPE tokenizer, tokenizing "a" + " " + "b" returns a different subword count than "a" + "\n" + "b" ; embedding a query with the query prompt versus the passage prompt reorders which document has the N N th-highest cosine similarity. Agent pitfall: The agent implemented the requested behavior behind an idiomatically-named class, function, or registry key instead of the exact public identifier and signature the task states, so the code builds and runs under its own tests but the checker never reaches it. Trigger: A hidden checker imports or instantiates a documented identifier (a service class name, a package function, a module registry key) or calls a documented public entrypoint with a stated signature; any differently-named or re-signatured variant is invisible to it even though it behaves correctly in isolation. Concrete correction: Before writing code, enumerate the exact public identifiers the prompt names—class name, function name, full parameter list and return type, registry key—and name the artifacts precisely; keep existing public entrypoints and signatures unchanged and add new internals around them rather than renaming the reachable surface. Tiny verification: from module import ExactName resolves only when the class/function is literally ExactName ; a class NearbyName that subclasses the expected type is not found by an importer that looks up ExactName .
